newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - March 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - March 31.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Monday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* Ascend Communications said it agreed to acquire Cascade Communications in a stock swap valued at $3.7 billion.
* Reinsurer PartnerRe is set to unveil a deal to buy Societe Anonyme Francaise de Reasurances from Swiss Re RUKZ.S for $950 million.
* Investors are looking for safety by buying shares in large companies with steady earnings potential.
* Bonds are looking more attractive after the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond's yield moved above seven percent but analysts say the bond market could come under severe pressure in the next month.
* Retailers are shifting away from reporting monthly sales data because they are "overused" by investors.
* Instead of basing production on forecasts, Compaq will instead make business computers when they are ordered.
* Regulatory filings show Columbia/HCA earned more than $65 million this decade in the El Paso, Texas market.
* The Ontario Securities Commission is investigating Bre-X Minerals after shares sank on news a mine in Indonesia contained "insignificant" amounts of gold.
* Corporate profits from current production fell 1.1 percent in the fourth quarter compared to the third quarter.
* Walt Disney plans to launch a web service for children which would charge a monthly fee and would available exclusively on Microsoft on-line service.
* Budget cuts at Apple Computer have caused top researchers to leave and reduced research projects.
* Roger Enrico, chief executive of PepsiCo, got $2.2 million in salary and bonus in 1996, and options on 1.7 million shares.
* Times Mirror opted for a stockbased compensation plan for outside company directors instead of fixed pay.
* Wang Chief Executive Joseph Tucci got an $8 million "retention" bonus from the company after he declined to join Novell.
* St. Jude Medical is expected to announce a restructured agreement to buy Ventritex, which makes heart defribillators, for over $350 million.
* Hearst named Victor Ganzi executive vice president, making him a likely choice for CEO.
* Heard on the Street: Retail stocks are hot these days but more and more stores are moving to put an end to one of the retail investor's most heavily used tools: monthly sales figures.

* Recent weakness in bond prices has sent yields past the magical seven percent level and an increasing number of investors are turning their sights to bonds for the first time in many months. But while a repeat of 1994's string of devastating rate increases isn't likely, and bonds may outperform stocks during the rest of the year, analysts say the bond market will likely come under severe pressure during the next month.
((New York newsdesk 212-859-1610))
